chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when al-Ward, the brother of al-Kumayt, entered upon him and said, 'May God make me your ransom! I had selected seventy questions for you, but not one of them comes to my mind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Not even one, O Ward?' He said: 'Yes, one has come to my mind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?'
He said: 'The Word of God, Blessed and Exalted: "So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know" — who are they?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'We [are they].' I said: 'Is it upon us to ask you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it incumbent upon you to answer us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to us.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ: The People of the Reminder — a Quranic phrase (16:43) interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the Imams of Ahlulbayt, the authoritative custodians of religious knowledge
key_terms.ذَاكَ إِلَيْنَا: That is up to us — the Imam's assertion that while answering is their prerogative, it remains a matter of their own discretion, not an unconditional obligation
key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom/sacrifice — a common expression of deep reverence and devotion directed to the Imam

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Dhikr) mentioned in Quran 16:43 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Bakr al-Hadrami recounts a visit to Imam al-Baqir (AS) in which al-Ward, brother of the famous Shia poet al-Kumayt, asks about the identity of 'the People of the Reminder' in Quran 16:43. The Imam identifies himself and the Imams as 'the People of the Reminder,' confirming that the obligation to ask them is binding on believers, while reserving the decision to answer to the Imam's own discretion. This hadith is pivotal in establishing the Shia doctrine of the Imamate as the authoritative source of religious guidance referenced in the Quran.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Baker Al Hazramy who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Ward, a brother of Al-Kumeyt came over and he said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I had chosen seventy questions for you<sup>asws</sup>, I cannot recall even one from these’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And not even one, O Ward?’ He said, ‘Yes, I have recalled one of these’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is it?’
He said, ‘The Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [16:43] so ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know, who are they?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> are’. I said, ‘Is it upon us that we ask you?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Is it upon you<sup>asws</sup> that you<sup>asws</sup> answer us?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is up to us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Bakr al-Hadrami who has said the following.

“I was in the presence of Imam (a.s.) abu Ja‘far (a.s.) and al-Ward brother of al-Kumayt came to see him. He to the Imams (a.s.) said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, I have chosen seventy questions and I do not know the answer even for one of them.” The Imams (a.s.) said, “Not even one answer, O Ward?” He then said, “Yes, I do know the answer for one of them.” The Imams (a.s.) asked, “What is it then?”
He replied, “It is the words of Allah that say, ‘Ask the people of Dhikr if you do not know’ who are they?”

The Imams (a.s.) replied, “We are the people of Dhikr?” I then said, “Must we then ask you?” The Imams (a.s.) said, “Yes, you must ask us for answers.” I then asked, “Must you then give us answers?” The Imams (a.s.) said, “We may or may not answer.”
